newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sodra says NorScan up 70,000 tonnes in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Sodra says NorScan up 70,000 tonnes in Feb.

text.p: Swedish non-traded forestry group Sodra Skogsagarna said on Thursday that North American and Scandinavian (NorScan) pulp stocks rose 70,000 tonnes in February from January to more than 2.1 million tonnes.
"This was the level people had expected," Tom Almgren, president of Sodra's unit Sodra Cell, told Reuters.
Pulp stocks usually rise in the winter and the figure is not seen affecting prices.
"This will have a neutral impact on pulp prices," he said.
Canadian pulp stocks increased the most in February, up 49,000 tonnes, while U.S. stocks rose 24,000 tonnes and Swedish stocks increased by 1,000 tonnes.
In Finland, pulp stocks fell by 4,000, Almgren said.
The forestry sector was up 1.32 percent on the Stockholm Stock Exchange at 1030 GMT, after being down 0.71 percent early on.
